notes.RS: Deng's 'stability overrides everything' (1989) and Đổi Mới's priority on political stability make order the main ground of authority: 2.
notes.CI: Integralism holds that rulers are legitimate only in subordination to the Church's spiritual end, not for keeping peace: -3.
notes.AC: Kropotkin and Malatesta hold that nobody owes obedience to rulers, whatever order they claim to keep: -3.
notes.MO: The Mohist origin story (Shang Tong) has people in a pre-political war of all against all, ended by choosing a ruler whose standards all follow: 2.

army.4.why: Divides the armed-citizenry camps (American conservatives, libertarians, Jeffersonian and classical republicans, anarchists, Calvinist resistance theory, guerrilla and workers-militia traditions) from state-monopoly camps (Hobbesians, Legalists, Leninist and fascist states, military rulers) and from pacifists (Tolstoyans, Gandhians, engaged Buddhists) who reject lethal force even against tyranny.

notes.AMC: The Second Amendment's purpose, in Goldwater-Reagan conservatism and the NRA tradition, is a check on tyranny as well as self-defence: 3.
notes.JR: Jefferson's 'tree of liberty must be refreshed from time to time with the blood of patriots' and the yeoman militia ideal make an armed citizenry the guard of freedom: 3.
notes.CLR: Machiavelli's Art of War and Discourses insist that free republics rest on citizens bearing their own arms rather than mercenaries: 3.
notes.HS: Leviathan ch. 21 denies any right to resist the sovereign; a private right to arms against him dissolves the covenant: -3.
notes.LE: Shang Yang's Book wants a weak people and strong state, with arms in the state's hands alone: -3.
notes.CA: Tolstoy and Dorothy Day take the Sermon on the Mount as forbidding violence, even against a tyrant: -3.
notes.GAN: Gandhi's satyagraha makes nonviolent noncooperation the answer to oppression; though he deplored the Arms Act's disarming of Indians, he rejected violent resistance as a creed: -2.
notes.GU: Foco theory and Che's guerrilla war rest on armed people overthrowing an abusive government: 2.
notes.SDD: Swiss militia soldiers keep their service rifles at home as part of citizen defence; the tradition is tied to freedom from tyranny: 2.
notes.JA: The Jacobin Constitution of 1793 (Art. 35) made insurrection the most sacred duty when government violates the people's rights: 2, split.
